title: How Well Do LLMs Perform in Peer Review? Evidence from Finance and Accounting
abstract: arXiv:2610.18435v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Referees increasingly use large language models (LLMs), while finance and accounting journals disagree about whether to allow it. We ask which part of a referee's job the models can do. GPT-4o, whose training data end before the 2024 conference season, referees the papers presented at the 2024 AFA and NBER finance meetings, and we compare its verdicts with publication in the top-three finance journals over the next two years. Papers the model scores one standard deviation higher are 44\% more likely to be published, net of author reputation. The result is not driven by look-ahead bias, as the model does not recall the outcomes. The information comes from its judgements of correctness and exposition. Its judgements of originality and significance carry none, and a referee guide that stresses importance does not help. translated_title: 大语言模型在同行评审中表现如何？来自金融学与会计学的证据
translated_abstract: 审稿人越来越多地使用大语言模型（LLM），而金融学和会计学期刊对于是否允许这样做意见不一。我们探究模型能够胜任审稿人工作的哪些部分。GPT-4o（其训练数据截止于2024年会议季之前）对2024年AFA和NBER金融会议上报告的论文进行了评审，我们将它的评审结论与随后两年内这些论文在三大顶级金融期刊上的发表情况进行了对比。在剔除作者声誉因素后，模型评分每高出一个标准差，论文被发表的概率就高出44%。该结果并非由前瞻偏差驱动，因为模型并不记得这些发表结果。其信息含量来自模型对正确性和表述质量的判断；而其对原创性和重要性的判断则不含信息量，强调重要性的审稿指南也无济于事。正确性与贡献之间的这种分化同样适用于会计学论文以及更新的模型GPT-5。LLM可以检查……
tldr: 研究发现GPT-4o评审金融论文时，其对正确性和写作质量的判断能显著预测论文能否发表在顶级期刊（评分每高一个标准差，发表概率提升44%），但其对原创性和重要性的判断则毫无预测力，且该结论在会计论文和GPT-5上同样成立。
en_tdlr: GPT-4o's referee judgments of correctness and exposition significantly predict publication in top finance journals (a one-standard-deviation higher score raises publication odds by 44%), while its judgments of originality and significance carry no predictive information, a pattern that holds for accounting papers and GPT-5 as well.
